zh.caption: 圖 1｜醫院報到的三種設計問題
zh.description: UI、HCI、UX 是並列的分析視角；使用者的目標是順利就醫。

items.title: UI — User Interface（使用者介面）
items.body:
報到機螢幕上的按鈕、字體、顏色、文字提示、插卡指示等，應該如何呈現？

例如：「確認報到」按鈕是否太小？長輩能不能看清楚？

items.title: HCI — Human–Computer Interaction（人機互動）
items.body:
人如何理解機器的指示、判斷下一步，以及操作機器？

例如：畫面寫著「完成」，病人以為已經看診報到，但系統其實只確認健保卡讀取成功。為什麼會誤解？

items.title: UX — User Experience（使用者經驗）
items.body:
從到醫院、報到、候診、看診、領藥到離院，整體經驗好不好？

例如：報到機操作只要 20 秒，但報到後沒有告訴病人診間在哪裡，病人還是可能迷路。

zh.caption: 圖 2｜HCI、UI、UX 與互動設計的交會
zh.description: 參考 Figma 的概念示意。交疊表示關注點互相影響，不是嚴格的學術集合分類，也不表示三個先後階段。

items.title: HCI｜人機互動
items.body: 人的認知、行為與互動能力

items.title: UI｜使用者介面
items.body: 畫面、控制元件與回應

items.title: UX｜使用者經驗
items.body: 整段服務的需求、結果與感受

items.title: IxD｜互動設計
items.body: 設計互動行為與回饋，涉及三種觀點的交會

zh.caption: 圖 3｜從使用者目標到整體結果
zh.description: 簡化的教學流程。實際操作通常會反覆經過「操作、回饋、理解、再操作」的循環；HCI 與 UX 也涵蓋比圖中更廣的範圍。 UI 與 HCI 為並列觀點，沒有先後順序；箭頭表示本圖的閱讀方向。

items.title: 使用者目標
items.body: 例如：完成銀行帳戶開立

items.title: UI：看見與操作
items.body: 表單、按鈕、資料提示、結果畫面

items.title: HCI：理解與判斷
items.body: 理解指示、選擇動作、解讀系統回饋

items.title: 系統處理與回饋
items.body: 檢查資料、儲存、通知、處理錯誤

items.title: UX：從開始到後續服務的整體結果
items.body: 是否完成開戶？過程是否順利？後續是否能使用帳戶？

zh.caption: 圖 4｜原本的設計與候選修改
zh.description: 兩個示意介面並列比較；按鈕是示意文字。候選修改仍須透過真人任務測試驗證。

items.title: 原本的設計
items.body:
成功！

操作完成

確定

不清楚是什麼成功，也不知道是否已正式送件。

items.title: 候選修改
items.body:
欄位檢查完成

3 個必要欄位已齊全。

尚未正式受理。

匯出檢查報告

清楚說明已完成的事項及下一步，但仍須測試。

en.caption: Figure 1 | Three design questions at hospital check-in
en.description: UI, HCI and UX are parallel perspectives; the user wants to receive medical care smoothly.

items.title: UI — User Interface
items.body:
How should buttons, typography, colors, prompts and card-insertion instructions appear on the kiosk?

For example: is “Confirm check-in” too small? Can older people read it?

items.title: HCI — Human–Computer Interaction
items.body:
How do people understand the instructions, decide what to do next and operate the kiosk?

For example: “Completed” makes a patient think check-in is done, but the system has only read the insurance card. Why does this misunderstanding happen?

items.title: UX — User Experience
items.body:
How is the whole experience of arrival, check-in, waiting, consultation, medication collection and departure?

For example: kiosk operation takes only 20 seconds, but the patient still gets lost because no consultation-room directions are given.

en.caption: Figure 2 | Where HCI, UI, UX and interaction design meet
en.description: A conceptual illustration after Figma. Overlap indicates interacting concerns, not a strict academic classification of sets or three successive phases.

items.title: HCI | Human–computer interaction
items.body: Human cognition, behavior and interaction capabilities

items.title: UI | User interface
items.body: Screens, controls and responses

items.title: UX | User experience
items.body: Needs, outcomes and feelings across the service

items.title: IxD | Interaction design
items.body: Design interaction behavior and feedback where the three perspectives meet

en.caption: Figure 3 | From a user goal to the overall outcome
en.description: A simplified teaching structure. Real use often cycles through action, feedback, interpretation and further action; HCI and UX extend beyond the scope shown here. UI and HCI are parallel perspectives, with no order between them; arrows indicate the reading direction of this illustration.

items.title: User goal
items.body: For example: open a bank account

items.title: UI: see and operate
items.body: Forms, buttons, information prompts and result screens

items.title: HCI: understand and decide
items.body: Interpret instructions, choose actions and interpret feedback

items.title: System processing and feedback
items.body: Check information, save, notify and handle errors

items.title: UX: overall outcome from start to follow-up service
items.body: Was the account opened? Was the process smooth? Can the account actually be used?

en.caption: Figure 4 | Original design and candidate change
en.description: Two illustrative interfaces for comparison; the buttons are illustrative text. The candidate still requires human task testing.

items.title: Original design
items.body:
Success!

Operation completed

OK

It is unclear what succeeded or whether the application was formally submitted.

items.title: Candidate change
items.body:
Field check completed

3 required fields are complete.

Not officially accepted yet.

Export check report

It explains what has completed and the next action, but still needs testing.
